############################################################
# 00_make_count_matrix.R
#
# Purpose:
#   Import individual HTSeq .count files and combine them
#   into one gene-by-sample count matrix.
#
# Input:
#   One .count file per sample
#
# Output:
#   countmtx.csv
#   sessionInfo_00_make_count_matrix.txt
############################################################


# ==========================================================
# 1. USER SETTINGS
# ==========================================================

# ---- Project directory ----
# CHANGE THIS to the main directory of your own project.
project_dir <- "YOUR/PROJECT/DIRECTORY/HERE"

# Folder containing the individual .count files.
# Change "Counts" only if your folder has a different name.
count_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "Counts")

# File extension used for the count files.
count_file_pattern <- "\\.count$"

# Name of the output count matrix.
output_file <- "countmtx.csv"


# ==========================================================
# 2. LOAD PACKAGES
# ==========================================================

library(dplyr)


# ==========================================================
# 3. CHECK DIRECTORIES
# ==========================================================

# Check whether the project directory exists.
if (!dir.exists(project_dir)) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "Project directory does not exist:\n",
      project_dir,
      "\n\nPlease update 'project_dir' in the USER SETTINGS section."
    )
  )
}

# Check whether the count-file directory exists.
if (!dir.exists(count_dir)) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "Count directory does not exist:\n",
      count_dir,
      "\n\nPlease check 'count_dir' in the USER SETTINGS section."
    )
  )
}

# Set the project directory as working directory.
setwd(project_dir)


# ==========================================================
# 4. IDENTIFY COUNT FILES
# ==========================================================

count_files <- list.files(
  path = count_dir,
  pattern = count_file_pattern,
  recursive = TRUE,
  full.names = TRUE
)

# Stop if no count files are found.
if (length(count_files) == 0) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "No count files matching ",
      count_file_pattern,
      " were found in:\n",
      count_dir
    )
  )
}

# Report number of files found.
message(
  "Number of count files found: ",
  length(count_files)
)

# Display sample file names.
print(basename(count_files))


# ==========================================================
# 5. FUNCTION TO READ ONE COUNT FILE
# ==========================================================

read_count_file <- function(file) {

  counts <- read.delim(
    file,
    header = FALSE,
    row.names = 1,
    check.names = FALSE
  )

  # Check that the file contains at least two data columns.
  # The original workflow used the second data column as
  # the gene-count column.
  if (ncol(counts) < 2) {
    stop(
      paste0(
        "Count file contains fewer than two data columns:\n",
        file
      )
    )
  }

  # Keep the second data column, as in the original workflow.
  counts <- counts[, 2, drop = FALSE]

  # Derive the sample name from the filename.
  sample_name <- sub(
    count_file_pattern,
    "",
    basename(file)
  )

  colnames(counts) <- sample_name

  return(counts)
}


# ==========================================================
# 6. READ ALL COUNT FILES
# ==========================================================

count_list <- lapply(
  count_files,
  read_count_file
)


# ==========================================================
# 7. QUALITY CHECKS BEFORE COMBINING
# ==========================================================

# ---- Check 1: sample names must be unique ----

sample_names <- vapply(
  count_list,
  function(x) colnames(x)[1],
  character(1)
)

if (anyDuplicated(sample_names) > 0) {

  duplicated_samples <- unique(
    sample_names[duplicated(sample_names)]
  )

  stop(
    paste0(
      "Duplicate sample names detected:\n",
      paste(duplicated_samples, collapse = ", "),
      "\n\nCheck the filenames of the .count files."
    )
  )
}


# ---- Check 2: all files must contain the same genes ----

reference_genes <- rownames(count_list[[1]])

same_genes <- vapply(
  count_list,
  function(x) {
    identical(
      rownames(x),
      reference_genes
    )
  },
  logical(1)
)

if (!all(same_genes)) {

  problematic_files <- basename(
    count_files[!same_genes]
  )

  stop(
    paste0(
      "Gene identifiers and/or gene order differ between count files.\n",
      "Problematic files:\n",
      paste(problematic_files, collapse = "\n"),
      "\n\nCount files should contain the same genes in the same order."
    )
  )
}


# ---- Check 3: gene identifiers should be unique ----

if (anyDuplicated(reference_genes) > 0) {

  duplicated_genes <- unique(
    reference_genes[duplicated(reference_genes)]
  )

  warning(
    paste0(
      "Duplicated gene identifiers were detected in the count files.\n",
      "Number of duplicated identifiers: ",
      length(duplicated_genes)
    )
  )
}


# ---- Check 4: counts should be numeric ----

all_numeric <- all(
  vapply(
    count_list,
    function(x) is.numeric(x[[1]]),
    logical(1)
  )
)

if (!all_numeric) {
  stop(
    "At least one count file contains non-numeric count values."
  )
}


# ---- Check 5: counts should not contain missing values ----

contains_na <- any(
  vapply(
    count_list,
    function(x) anyNA(x),
    logical(1)
  )
)

if (contains_na) {
  stop(
    "Missing values were detected in one or more count files."
  )
}


# ---- Check 6: counts should not be negative ----

contains_negative <- any(
  vapply(
    count_list,
    function(x) any(x[[1]] < 0),
    logical(1)
  )
)

if (contains_negative) {
  stop(
    "Negative count values were detected. Raw read counts should not be negative."
  )
}


# ==========================================================
# 8. COMBINE COUNT FILES
# ==========================================================

countmtx <- do.call(
  cbind,
  count_list
)


# ==========================================================
# 9. FINAL COUNT-MATRIX CHECKS
# ==========================================================

message(
  "Count matrix successfully created."
)

message(
  "Number of genes: ",
  nrow(countmtx)
)

message(
  "Number of samples: ",
  ncol(countmtx)
)

# Inspect the first rows.
print(
  head(countmtx)
)

# Inspect sample names.
print(
  colnames(countmtx)
)

# Check library sizes.
library_sizes <- colSums(countmtx)

print(
  data.frame(
    Sample = names(library_sizes),
    Library_size = library_sizes
  )
)

# Warn about samples with zero total counts.
if (any(library_sizes == 0)) {

  warning(
    paste0(
      "The following samples have a library size of zero:\n",
      paste(
        names(library_sizes)[library_sizes == 0],
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  )
}


# ==========================================================
# 10. SAVE COUNT MATRIX
# ==========================================================

output_path <- file.path(
  project_dir,
  output_file
)

write.csv(
  countmtx,
  file = output_path,
  row.names = TRUE
)

message(
  "Count matrix saved to:\n",
  output_path
)


# ==========================================================
# 11. SAVE SESSION INFORMATION
# ==========================================================

session_file <- file.path(
  project_dir,
  "sessionInfo_00_make_count_matrix.txt"
)

capture.output(
  sessionInfo(),
  file = session_file
)

message(
  "Session information saved to:\n",
  session_file
)
